name: Node.js 22 + TypeScript + Electron desktop
summary: Re-platform WinForms / WPF / console / library code onto a cross-platform Electron desktop app written in TypeScript. Business logic lives in the main process (or a Node worker/local service) behind a typed IPC API; the UI is a React renderer. Server-side parts (Web API, WCF, workers) may be ported to Node services with the same stack.

stack.Desktop shell: Electron (current stable) with contextIsolation, sandboxed renderer, preload-exposed typed IPC
stack.UI: React 18 + Vite; component library: Fluent UI React (closest to WinForms/WPF look) or MUI
stack.State: Zustand or Redux Toolkit; forms with React Hook Form + Zod
stack.Persistence: Prisma ORM (SQL Server / PostgreSQL / SQLite) or Kysely for hand-written SQL; better-sqlite3 for local stores
stack.Validation: Zod schemas shared between main and renderer
stack.Testing: Vitest (unit), Playwright for Electron (UI/E2E), Testcontainers for Node (integration)

projectLayout: packages/domain/        pure TS: entities, value objects, business rules (no Electron/Node deps)
packages/application/   use cases (one per legacy flow), ports
packages/infrastructure/ Prisma/Kysely repositories, messaging, cache, HTTP clients
apps/desktop/main/      Electron main process: window management, IPC handlers → use cases
apps/desktop/renderer/  React screens (one per legacy Form/Window), routing = legacy navigation
tests/parity/           characterization tests replaying legacy golden cases
conventions: One React screen per legacy Form/Window/Page; keep field names and tab order from the legacy screen inventory.
Each legacy event handler / command becomes an IPC call `capability:action` that invokes an application use case; no business logic in the renderer.
Every legacy business rule becomes a named function in packages/domain with a Vitest test tagged with the BR id.
Use decimal.js (or big.js) for money/decimal math; never JS number. Map MidpointRounding.ToEven ⇒ Decimal.ROUND_HALF_EVEN.
Dates: Temporal polyfill or date-fns with explicit time zones; .NET DateTime.Kind decisions recorded in research.md.
Renderer is sandboxed: nodeIntegration=false, contextIsolation=true; validate all IPC payloads with Zod.
Windows-specific dependencies (registry, COM, WMI, printers) go behind platform adapters with a Windows implementation via native modules or a helper process.
testing: Characterization tests per legacy flow (drive legacy app with recorded inputs, assert outputs and persisted state) must pass before cut-over.
Playwright for Electron reproduces each user journey end to end.
Testcontainers for databases and brokers in integration tests.
Visual regression for screens with dense forms/grids where layout parity matters.
nonFunctional: Cold start under 3 s on reference hardware; long operations off the UI thread (worker_threads / utility process).
Offline behaviour matches legacy (local cache/queue if legacy worked offline).
